units.translation: ⟦1⟧ must, just as at 1027, mean a festive procession; accordingly, women were predominantly involved in this cult; for ⟦2⟧ cannot well be dependent on ⟦3⟧.

⟦1⟧ aorist, see on ⟦2⟧, 'you can obtain' (⟦3⟧ 869). Lines 858–866 or 869 are excised by some (Dindorf, Wecklein) as an interpolation, especially because they interrupt the connection. But it is fitting that Athena now also speaks of the Eumenides' return service, and only thus can the summing up be correctly made (868): ⟦4⟧, ⟦5⟧. Here the return service is expressed only negatively, as abstention from harm (differently after the reconciliation, 903 ff.); the Erinyes have indeed no longer threatened, but they have not retracted their threat, which is why similar things stand in the following speech, 888 f. — Because in the Teubner text edition the order is changed: 858–866 after 912, which seems to me even more wrong: after the reconciliation has taken place, such hostile activity of the Erinyes can no longer be spoken of at all.
Line 859 ⟦1⟧ whetstone (⟦2⟧ ⟦3⟧) in another transferred use ⟦4⟧; cf. ⟦5⟧ ⟦6⟧, ⟦7⟧ ⟦8⟧ Alcidamas in Aristotle Rhetoric 3, 3, p. 1406 a 9.
sharpened by the unmixed anger of his thought

The ⟦1⟧, as the seat of the emotions, are, as it were, sharpened and thereby become bloody, and the angry person is provoked to bloodshed. Such disturbances were thus attributed to the angered spirits of the deep.

⟦1⟧ need not be made dependent on ⟦2⟧, but can be an attribute, cf. ⟦3⟧ ⟦4⟧ ⟦5⟧⟦6⟧ (iuvenilis Ddf.). But impossible is ⟦7⟧ (M perhaps first -⟦8⟧) ⟦9⟧, from which (after ⟦10⟧ ⟦11⟧) is easily restored ⟦12⟧, raging surges of anger, such as can come from wine, but are produced by the avenging spirits without wine.
with wineless maddening surges of anger
⟦1⟧ —, ◡ ◡ like ⟦2⟧ 797, ⟦3⟧ 107, ⟦4⟧ ⟦5⟧. — Weil quotes from Goethe: Trunken müssen wir alle sein, Jugend ist Trunkenheit ohne Wein.
